## 🎬 See it in action

<p align="center"><img src="assets/auralloy-demo.gif" alt="Auralloy demo" width="100%"></p>

<p align="center"><sub>Intro, import, automatic analysis, Forge, a sequential mix, one-click Slowed + Reverb, export.</sub></p>

<a id="what"></a>

## ✨ What it does

| | |
|---|---|
| 🎛️ **Forge: automatic mashups** | Pick two or more songs. Auralloy matches tempo and key, then plays them one after another, beat-matched, with a smooth blend at every switch. |
| 🔎 **Explainable by design** | Every decision follows a written rule and is logged in plain language. No black box. |
| 🎚️ **Studio: a real editor** | Multi-track timeline with snapping, split, trim, fades, reverse, per-clip gain, tempo and pitch, loop regions and unlimited undo. |
| 🌧️ **Slowed + reverb and lofi** | One-click looks and a full effects rack: EQ, lofi tape, compressor, chorus, echo, reverb, width, rain and vinyl. |
| 💎 **High-quality export** | WAV 16/24/32-bit float, FLAC and MP3 at 44.1 to 96 kHz, processed in 32-bit float. |
| 🧪 **Open and tested** | AGPL-3.0, headless tests, a seeded benchmark suite and a research preprint. |

## 🧭 How it works

<p align="center"><img src="assets/pipeline.svg" alt="pipeline" width="100%"></p>

1. Analyse tempo, beats, bars, key and sections.
2. Split stems: vocals, drums, bass, other.
3. Plan the arrangement with the mashup rules and write the log.
4. Render every clip with matched tempo and pitch.
5. Edit: everything is an ordinary clip on the timeline.

<a id="start"></a>

## 🚀 Get started

1. Download <b>Auralloy-0.0.1-windows-x64.zip</b> from Releases and run <code>Auralloy.exe</code>.
2. Drop two or more songs into the window.
3. Open <b>Forge</b> and press the orb: the songs play one after another.
4. Edit on the timeline, pick a look, then <b>Export</b>.

<details>
<summary><b>Build from source (Windows)</b></summary>

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 (C++ workload) or Build Tools, CMake 3.22+, git.

```bash
cmake -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64          # fetches JUCE at a pinned commit
cmake --build build --config Release --target Auralloy
# -> build/Auralloy_artefacts/Release/Auralloy.exe
```

Use an existing JUCE checkout with `-DAURALLOY_JUCE_DIR=path/to/JUCE`. Run the tests with `-DAURALLOY_TESTS=ON`; regenerate the brand assets and the demo with `-DAURALLOY_TOOLS=ON`.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Keyboard shortcuts</b></summary>

`Space` play · `S` split · `Del` delete · `Ctrl+D` duplicate · `Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y` undo / redo · `Alt+Z` undo a sound change · `L` loop · `B` FX bypass · `F` fit · `+ / -` zoom · `1 / 2` Studio / Forge · `Ctrl+O` add songs · `Ctrl+E` export · `Ctrl+S` save.

Timeline: wheel = zoom, `Ctrl`+wheel = pan, `Shift`+drag = loop region, double-click a clip = loop it. Knobs: hover + mouse wheel (`Shift` = fine), double-click = reset.

</details>

<a id="rules"></a>

## 📐 The mashup rules

Forge follows explicit rules and writes a plain-language log of every decision.

- One shared tempo, with the least time-stretching.
- One shared key (A minor equals C major), with the smallest pitch shift.
- Every cut on a downbeat, in 4-bar phrases.
- One vocal and one bass at a time; the bass swaps on a bar line.
- Sections matched by energy; blends of 2 to 8 bars.
- Every song keeps its own balance and is level-matched.

Details: [docs/RULES.md](docs/RULES.md)

<a id="bench"></a>

## 📊 Benchmarks

Seeded, synthetic and reproducible (see benchmarks/). Real music will be messier.

| | |
|---|---:|
| Tempo within 0.5 % | **93.8 %** |
| Key exact or relative | **99.0 %** |
| Downbeat within 50 ms | **85.4 %** |
| Section boundaries (F1) | **0.71** |
| Rule compliance | **100.0 %** |
| Rendered tempo error | **0.010 BPM** |
| Tempo drift vs naive crossfade | **0.05 vs 3.07 BPM** |

<sub>96 songs · 45 planned mashups · stems SI-SDR vocals 21.9 dB, drums -0.3 dB, bass 6.9 dB · seed 20261101</sub>

## ⚠️ Honest limitations

- Assumes a mostly steady 4/4 tempo.
- Quick Stems is classic DSP, not a neural separator.
- Key detection can be wrong on ambiguous harmony.
- Validated on synthetic songs; real music needs more testing.

<a id="faq"></a>

## ❓ FAQ

<details>
<summary><b>How many songs do I need?</b></summary>

At least two, and there is no upper limit. Songs whose tempo is more than 15 % away from the shared target, or whose key needs more than 3 semitones of shift, are left out, and the log tells you which and why.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Is there AI or a cloud service involved?</b></summary>

No. Auralloy is classic signal processing plus written rules. It runs locally, needs no GPU and makes no network connections.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How good is the stem separation?</b></summary>

Quick Stems is a lightweight DSP separator: decent for a centred lead vocal and bass, weak for drums. A neural separator can replace it behind one function. See the benchmark numbers above.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Will it work on my real music?</b></summary>

It was validated on synthetic songs only; real recordings are harder (see *Honest limitations*). Please report what goes wrong with an issue.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Which platforms are supported?</b></summary>

The release is Windows x64. The code is portable C++17 on JUCE, but macOS and Linux builds are untested.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Can I mash up copyrighted songs?</b></summary>

Auralloy is a tool. You are responsible for the rights to the audio you import and for what you publish.

</details>
